prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mathematics (elementary differential equations, vector fields and operators).
Basic knowledge of mechanics (mechanics of a point particle).
Participation certificate for a 'ijkingstoets' (placement test) is required to follow courses in the Bachelor of Engineering Science and Bachelor of Engineering Science: Architecture programs.

learning_outcomes.text: The student can precisely formulate the relevant concepts and basic laws of physics and derive their interrelationships.

The student can apply the acquired insights, knowledge of studied laws and basic properties to analyze and computationally solve concrete problems that manifest in various subfields of engineering sciences.
The student is able to explain the working principle of various important devices and apparatus relevant to engineers.

syllabus_topics: Detection of sound waves - intensity and loudness
Heat, thermal expansion and kinetic gas theory
Kinetic gas theory and ideal gas law
Matter, waves and energy – introduction to concepts of quantum mechanics
Matter waves (duality of particles and waves)
Wavelength of a matter particle (de Broglie's idea)
Application: spectra of atoms and molecules
Wave-particle duality extended to massless particles
Absorption, emission and stimulated emission of photons
Applications: discrete (atomic gas) as well as continuous spectra (solids)
Applications: nuclear fission and nuclear fusion
Electric field of a charge distribution (charged ring, wire, disk,…)
Torque on an electric dipole in an external electric field
Applications of Gauss's law (charged sphere, wire, plate,…)
Electric potential energy and electric potential
Coulomb's law for the electric potential of a point charge
Electric potential of a charge distribution
The sharp point effect and lightning rods
Series and parallel connections of capacitors
Polarization of a dielectric and influence on the properties of capacitors
Series and parallel connections of resistors
Magnetic force on a current and on a moving charge
Motion of an electron in a magnetic field
Charge velocity filter and mass spectrometer
Torque on a current loop and principle of an electric motor
Ampère's law and applications (B field of wire, solenoid, toroid,…)
Biot-Savart law and applications (B field of a current loop, straight wire,…)
Magnetic materials and origin of ferromagnetism
Induced EMF by a changing magnetic flux and Faraday's law
Transformers and transport of electrical power
Ampère-Maxwell law and Gauss's law for magnetism
Maxwell's equations - integral and differential forms
Light as an electromagnetic wave – the electromagnetic spectrum
Energy in electromagnetic waves and the Poynting vector
Reflection and refraction of light (Snell's law)
Intensity of light in the interference pattern
Circular apertures and resolution of a lens

assessment_methods.method: Written exam during the examination period

assessment_rules: The written exam consists of two theory questions, possibly with application, and three or four exercises, all as open questions. Students whose native language is not Dutch may use one non-technical translating dictionary during evaluations, after prior notification to the ombuds by specific deadlines.
